text:
Rasmus Dahlin is off to a slower start than usual, as The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn put it this week, and the numbers agree without sounding any alarm. He has 11 points in 16 games on 24:37 a night, six of them on the power play, and only one goal in his last ten. For a defenseman Evolving-Hockey ranked 12th of 215 last season, that's a quiet line.

The process is still there. Buffalo has had 53.6% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, four points better than when he sits, and his finishing and on-ice luck are both right around neutral. Our talent range puts his true scoring rate above what he's showing, so the points look more likely to catch up than the play is to slip.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists last season, and carrying the puck in on 42% of his entries. In a tight division race, watch whether those setups start turning into goals for the forwards around him.
headline: Dahlin's quieter start
